Soojin — draft manifest attached (see redwood_model_manifest_v1.json). Key fields included (brief):

- model_id: human-readable catalog id
- model_version: semantic tag (stable/pin ID)
- model_hash: sha256 of artifact used for inference
- license: SPDX or text fallback (we include SPDX where available)
- derived_from: list of upstream model ids + commit/weights provenance (when available)
- quantization_profile: recommended runtime profile (q4_0, q8_0 etc)
- earliest_deprecation_date: ISO (if scheduled)
- pin_recommendation: consumer-facing guidance (e.g., use pinned version to avoid breaking changes)
- attribution_statement: minimal attribution text to surface in audit logs

Notes: we include an attestation field for curated models where we can provide a scanned SBOM-like list of licenses for tokenizer and model weight sources. For strictly upstream-open models we include links to the original release and SPDX where possible.

Hi Amit — thanks for the follow-up. Attached are the artifacts we discussed: a short example model manifest, our deprecation playbook, and a compact RFI attachments table for your procurement/legal team. Summary below.

1) Example manifest (redwood_model_manifest_v1.json) — contains the fields we typically publish with a catalog release. Example provenance tokens include upstream_release_url, weights_checksum, and optional source_commit. When upstream metadata is lacking we mark provenance as "unverified" and include guidance for customers.

2) Deprecation playbook (deprecation_playbook.pdf) — condensed steps we follow when a model variant is scheduled for removal or incompatible update:
   - Notification window: 30 days for hosted catalog-only variants; 90 days for Dedicated customers with pinned capacity by contract (we can negotiate longer windows in enterprise SOWs).
   - Pinning semantics: customers can pin a model_version id (immutable snapshot) which Redwood will continue to serve for at least the contracted rollback window; pinned snapshots include a full manifest and a read-only tag.
   - Emergency removal: in the event of a licensing violation discovered post-release, we will notify immediately and provide a remediation plan. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer assisted migration and temporary rerouting to compatible variants where possible.
   - Rollback assistance: we maintain a 14-day rollback snapshot for recent variant updates (short-term safety net) plus archived pinned snapshots for contracted customers.

3) Procurement bullets (see attached RFI table) — short contract language we propose for attribution, license-change triggers, and remediation credits. Laura included an escalation contact and contact SLA.

Attachments: redwood_model_manifest_v1.json (example), deprecation_playbook.pdf (playbook), rfi_attachment_table.xlsx (procurement bullets)

Links: DocuSign addendum draft (https://docusign.com/somefolder/FS-0456), internal RFI ticket https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RFI-1224

Let us know if you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough of the manifest format; happy to schedule with Marissa.

Best,
